name: Elishah
overview: Elishah is a male figure identified as a son of Japheth according to Rahlfs' Septuaginta rendering of Genesis 10:2. This name does not appear in the traditional Masoretic Text (BHS Hebrew text), highlighting a textual variation in the biblical genealogies. No tribal affiliation or surname is recorded for Elishah in the available sources.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishah is presented as a proper name in the Septuagint version of Genesis 10:2. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to the name in the given data, so it is recognized simply as a personal name without additional significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Elishah as a son of Japheth, situating him within the genealogical line descending from Noah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections or descendants are recorded in the data provided.
scriptureSignificance: Elishah's mention in the Septuagint account of Genesis 10:2 contributes to the biblical record of the post-Flood genealogies, which outline the nations and peoples descended from Noah's sons. The presence of his name in the Septuagint but absence in the Hebrew text reflects the textual transmission history and variations in ancient manuscripts. Though not elaborated upon elsewhere, Elishah's inclusion underscores the completeness of Japheth's lineage as preserved in some biblical traditions.
